record.reply: Utilitarian evaluation now explicitly counts the welfare effect of promise-keeping.  The promise itself is a real fact (PROP:WORLD:RECOGNITION:4697fd89cd506cc4), but the scenario does not state how much utility fulfilment or breach carries.  That welfare increment therefore remains an un-quantified hypothesis.  Given the very large gap in expected survival (0.95 vs 0.05 = 0.90 expected life difference), an additional trust/credibility benefit would have to be at least 0.90 life-equivalents to reverse the ranking.  Ordinary estimates of relationship or institutional trust rarely approach the value of saving almost one whole life, so the expected-survivor calculus still dominates.  I therefore keep the preference for A0 while flagging the quantitative uncertainty about trust utility as a reversal boundary.
record.framework_commitment: Benthamite greatest-happiness principle: choose the act with the larger total expected welfare.
record.reasoning_bridge: 1. Expected lives saved: A0 = 0.95, A1 = 0.05 (grounded). 2. Promise-keeping adds some positive utility to A1 and some negative utility to A0, but magnitude is unstated. 3. Unless that magnitude ≥ 0.90 life-equivalents, A0 still maximises expected welfare. 4. Because this threshold is plausible but not established, note it as ft and gu boundary; scores unchanged.
record.remaining_uncertainty: Exact welfare value of broken promise to Cara and to wider social trust; any secondary effects on others.
record.reversal_condition: If the disutility of breaking the promise (or utility of keeping it) reached or exceeded 0.90 expected lives, A1 would become preferable.
